# Module-trait correlation

The maintained entry point is `run_module_trait_analysis()`. Advanced users
should call it directly from R code with explicit arguments:

```{r}
module_trait_result <- run_module_trait_analysis(
  session_dir = session_dir,
  continuous_traits = continuous_traits,
  categorical_variables = categorical_variables,
  reference_levels = reference_levels,
  network_types = c("hc", "kmeans"),
  continuous_method = "pearson",
  fit_categorical_models = TRUE,
  model_covariates = model_covariates
)
```

The remaining chunks preserve the earlier low-level implementation for
provenance only.

```{r}
load(file.path(session_dir, "out", "1_prepared_data.RData"))

network_result <- readRDS(
  file.path(session_dir, "out", "3_networks.rds")
)
net <- network_result$network
net_km <- network_result$network_kmeans
```

## Build binary contrast matrix for categorical variables testing

<https://peterlangfelder.com/2018/11/25/working-with-categorical-variables/>

Categorical variables and reference levels are read from the session parameters. When `categorical_variables` is `NULL`, factor, character, and logical metadata columns are detected automatically. All non-redundant contrasts are retained by default. Variables with fewer than two observed levels are reported and skipped because they cannot define a contrast.

```{r}
# Generate contrasts using stable variable and level names rather than column
# positions. get0() provides backward-compatible defaults for older sessions.
binary.matrix <- binary_contrast_matrix(
  data = data$metadata,
  variables = get0("categorical_variables", ifnotfound = NULL),
  reference_levels = get0("categorical_reference_levels", ifnotfound = NULL),
  includePairwise = get0("categorical_include_pairwise", ifnotfound = TRUE),
  vsAll = get0("categorical_include_vs_all", ifnotfound = TRUE),
  minCount = get0("categorical_min_count", ifnotfound = 1),
  drop_redundant = get0("categorical_drop_redundant", ifnotfound = TRUE)
)

binary.matrix <- select_binary_contrasts(
  binary_matrix = binary.matrix,
  include = get0("categorical_contrasts", ifnotfound = NULL),
  exclude = get0("categorical_exclude_contrasts", ifnotfound = NULL)
)

head(binary.matrix)

# Save the exact matrix used by the correlation analyses.
binary.matrix.output <- data.frame(
  sample = rownames(binary.matrix),
  binary.matrix,
  check.names = FALSE
)
readr::write_tsv(
  binary.matrix.output,
  file.path(session_dir, "out", "module_trait_binary_contrasts.tsv")
)
```

## Categorical variables (using Pearson correlation)

```{r}
corr.cat.var <- correlation_categorical_var(network = net, binary_matrix = binary.matrix)
corr.cat.var.km <- correlation_categorical_var(network = net_km, binary_matrix = binary.matrix)
```

```{r}
pdf(file = file.path(session_dir, "plots", "EMhc-condition_corr.pdf"),

plot(corr.cat.var.km$hm)
dev.off()
```

## Categorical variables (using linear model)

The Estimate for the binary predictor indicates the difference in the mean eigengene value between the two groups defined by the binary contrast.

```{r}
plot.type = "dotplot" #choose between dotplot or heatmap

pdf(file = file.path(session_dir, "plots", paste0("EMkm-condition_corr_lm_", plot.type, ".pdf")), 
  width = 10,          # Width in inches
  height = 16.18,         # Height in inches
  bg = "white")
correlation_categorical_var_lm(network = net_km, binary_matrix = binary.matrix, plot_type = plot.type)
dev.off()

pdf(file = file.path(session_dir, "plots", paste0("EMhc-condition_corr_lm_", plot.type, ".pdf")), 
  width = 10,          # Width in inches
  height = 16.18,         # Height in inches
  bg = "white")
correlation_categorical_var_lm(network = net, binary_matrix = binary.matrix, plot_type = plot.type)
dev.off()


```
